Hopefully voat doesn't get swamped again any time soon. :/ Anyway, here's the first sentence out of one of my favorite books when I was a young(er) man.

"In the late summer of that year we lived in a house in a village that looked across the river and the plain to the mountains."

- Ernest Hemingway, "A Farewell To Arms"

 

And some vaguely related vocabulary:
1. town
2. city
3. neighborhood
4. mountain (opp. mountain range)
5. live in (verb) (in the sense of inhabiting a place)

en the ul sumer a thet yur wi levdes en haza en tan xe luktet krauzda ria ayn playn che the shyerra.
/ɛn ðə ʌl sʌme˞ ə ðɛʔ je˞ː wi lɛvdəs ɛn hæːzə ɛn tæːn xə lʌːktəʔ kɹaʊzdə riə eɪn pləɪn tʃə ðə ʃje˞ɹə/
in the old summer of that year we lived-us in house en town that looked-it across river and plain to the mountains.

Rever /ɹɛve˞/ and ria /ɹiə/ both mean 'river', with really no distinction between the two.
Krauzda isn't followed by the definite article. It's directly from 'across(ed) the' so I guess it just sort of steals the definiteness from whatever follows it. Not sure how to explain it, but it is what it is.
'Plain' probably isn't a natural word for the people who speak this language. You could get away with saying the word for 'valley' (which escapes me right now), but 'plain' would be either playn as above or pelayn /pʰəˈləɪn/. The difference is minimal, but part of me wants to keep it an option... for reasons.

 

Extra vocab:
1. tan /tæːn/ (um. I'll just leave it. Feel free to pick another word)
2. sedi /sɛdi/
3. varyou /vɛɹjəʊ/
4. ma(n)ttn /mæː(n)ʔn̩/ (the mattnz = the shyerra)
5. che levya en /tʃə lɛvjə ɛn/ or che sxuwotya ɛn /tʃə sxəˈwaʔjə ɛn/
